faq.q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Resizing happens entirely in your browser, so your photos never leave your device and nothing is stored or logged.

faq.q: How do I resize without stretching or distorting the picture?
faq.a: Fill in only the width or only the height and the other side is worked out for you. With both filled in and Keep aspect ratio ticked, the picture is fitted inside that box without distortion.

faq.q: What is the difference between Fill, Fit and Stretch for ready-made sizes?
faq.a: Fill scales the picture until it covers the whole size and crops what overflows. Fit shows the whole picture and adds white bars if the shapes differ. Stretch forces the exact size and can distort the picture.

faq.q: Does enlarging an image make it sharper?
faq.a: No. Making an image larger cannot add detail that is not there, so it may look soft. For the best quality, start from the largest original you have.

faq.q: Why did my file size change so much?
faq.a: File size depends on the pixel dimensions, the format and the quality. Making an image smaller usually shrinks the file a lot, while a larger size or PNG output can make it bigger.
